caption: Sienelės storis, mm. / Teorinis metro svoris (kg/m).
notes: Units: first column = outer dimensions in mm (larger side x smaller side, as printed); the other column labels are wall thicknesses in mm; cell values = theoretical mass in kg per metre. The caption is a single merged header line above the wall-thickness labels (it does not belong to one column). Decimal separator is printed as a dot; all weights are printed with two decimals and trailing zeros are kept as printed. No footnotes. 21 body rows, 11 thickness columns, 112 filled value cells; every empty cell is empty in the source image. SOURCE ANOMALIES (all transcribed exactly as printed, NOT corrected; digits and cell positions verified pixel-exact): (1) row 160x80 / column 14.2 is printed "16.90" - smaller than every other value in that row (column 12.5 = 40.90), so the source looks wrong in this cell (it may be a value misplaced in the source; the cell 180x100 / 4.0 is empty in the image). (2) row 200x100: column 14.2 is empty while column 16.0 holds 65.20 (a gap inside the row). (3) row 180x100: column 4.0 is empty although the neighbouring rows 160x80 and 200x100 have a 4.0 value. (4) Row order is as printed: 150x100 comes before 160x80, so the weights in columns 4.0-12.5 drop between these two rows (15.10 -> 14.40 etc.); that is the source order, not a reading slip. Rows 350x250 and 400x200 carry identical weights in columns 8.0-16.0 (72.80, 90.20, 112.00, 126.00, 141.00), as printed. Informational self-check (no value was changed because of it): apart from the 16.90 cell, the other 111 printed values agree with the EN 10210-2 hot-finished formula at 7850 kg/m3 to three significant digits.
